title: Forward Exchange Coordination
name: Forward Exchange Coordination
metaTitle: Forward Exchange Coordination in Fort Worth, TX
metaDescription: Fort Worth forward 1031 exchange coordination: sequencing the relinquished sale, 45-day identification, and 180-day closing across Alliance and downtown deals.

sections.html: A forward exchange, also called a delayed exchange, is the standard structure where the relinquished property sells first and the replacement property closes afterward, within the 180-day period. Most Fort Worth investors trading Cultural District retail or Alliance industrial buildings use this structure because it does not require lining up a replacement before the current property sells.

sections.heading: Sequencing the Relinquished Sale
sections.html:
The relinquished sale closing date sets both the 45-day and 180-day clocks in motion simultaneously, so the exchange agreement with the qualified intermediary needs to be signed and the assignment documents in place before that closing, not after. On a downtown office sale, that means coordinating the exchange agreement alongside the standard closing documents rather than as an afterthought once funds are already in escrow.

Proceeds from the relinquished sale route directly to the qualified intermediary's escrow account, never to the taxpayer, which the closing instructions have to reflect precisely.

sections.heading: Managing the Identification and Closing Sequence
sections.html:
Once the relinquished sale closes, the forward exchange runs on its two fixed deadlines: identification by day 45, closing by day 180. Fort Worth investors sourcing an Alliance-area distribution building often use the early weeks of this window most intensively, since industrial product with BNSF rail access can move quickly once listed.

  • Confirm the exchange agreement is signed before the relinquished closing
  • Route proceeds to the qualified intermediary's escrow account at closing
  • Deliver written identification before the 45-day deadline
  • Close on the replacement property before the 180-day deadline

sections.heading: Coordinating Multiple Parties Across the Window
sections.html: A forward exchange typically involves the qualified intermediary, both sets of closing attorneys or title companies, and often a lender on the replacement side, all working against the same fixed calendar. Keeping those parties aligned on the deadline, particularly when a Southlake or Grapevine replacement purchase involves new financing, is the core coordination task.

sections.heading: When a Forward Exchange Is Not the Right Structure
sections.html: If a suitable replacement property is already under contract before the relinquished sale closes, or if the investor needs to acquire before selling, a reverse exchange structure may fit better than a forward exchange. That determination is made before the relinquished sale, since switching structures after closing is not possible.

sections.heading: Coordinating a Forward Exchange Alongside an Existing Fort Worth Portfolio
sections.html:
Investors who already hold other property in the Fort Worth area sometimes run a forward exchange while continuing to manage that existing portfolio, which means the exchange calendar has to be tracked independently from routine leasing and operational work rather than folded into it. A property manager focused on day-to-day operations at a Bedford or Euless asset is not necessarily watching the 45-day and 180-day deadlines the way the exchange coordination team is, so responsibility for the exchange calendar needs a clear owner.

That separation of duties matters most when the same principals are involved in both the ongoing portfolio and the exchange transaction, since a scheduling conflict or a missed notice can easily happen if calendar ownership is assumed rather than explicitly assigned.

Assigning a single point of contact for the exchange calendar, distinct from whoever handles day-to-day property management, gives the deal one owner accountable for the 45-day and 180-day deadlines regardless of what else is happening across the rest of the portfolio. That person is typically the one communicating directly with the qualified intermediary, the closing attorneys, and any lender involved, so deadline-related decisions are not made piecemeal by whichever team member happens to be handling a related task that week. That single point of contact also becomes the one who confirms, at each milestone, whether the exchange is still on pace for the 180-day deadline or whether an adjustment to the closing plan is needed. Where multiple principals hold an interest in the same relinquished property, that single point of contact also becomes the one who relays deadline-related decisions back to the group, so the exchange calendar is not delayed by internal coordination among the ownership group itself. That structure keeps the exchange moving on its statutory schedule even when the group behind the transaction has its own internal decision-making pace. Establishing that single point of contact at the very start of the forward exchange, before the relinquished property even goes to market, avoids scrambling to assign the role once the clock is already running.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a forward exchange and a reverse exchange?
faqs.a: A forward exchange sells the relinquished property first and acquires the replacement afterward. A reverse exchange acquires the replacement first, using a separate holding structure until the relinquished property sells.

faqs.q: When does the 180-day clock start on a Fort Worth forward exchange?
faqs.a: It starts on the closing date of the relinquished property, running simultaneously with the 45-day identification period rather than after it.

faqs.q: Does the exchange agreement need to be signed before the relinquished property closes?
faqs.a: Yes. The exchange agreement with the qualified intermediary needs to be in place before the relinquished closing so proceeds can route correctly at closing rather than to the taxpayer directly.

faqs.q: Can financing on the replacement property affect the forward exchange timeline?
faqs.a: Yes. Lender underwriting timelines are one of the more common reasons a replacement closing gets pushed close to the 180-day deadline, so financing is typically initiated as early in the window as possible.

faqs.q: Is a forward exchange the most common structure for Fort Worth investors?
faqs.a: Yes, it is the most commonly used structure since it does not require acquiring a replacement property before the current property has sold.
